capture.asset_override: VERSE_KIT_PACK selects the current production kit. No VERSE_KIT_UNPINNED flag is set.
capture.timing_scope: Continuous host iteration intervals, including simulation, camera and mesh preparation, encoding, submission, admission and artifact readback waits, retained-pixel copies, and bookkeeping. Adjacent starts bound each interval; the last ends after final drain. Every frame enters p99/max without filtering, retaining the 16.7 ms live budget. This is bounded throughput cadence; frame completion latency is reported separately.
capture.comparison_limits: Current production kit yields 509 chunks; historical DAE runs yield 700. No cap or code density is reduced. Source, asset, profile, and timing policy differences prevent a controlled historical speedup claim.

counter_limits: Missing counters and detect/solve timings are null. End body/collider record counts are not reported; only phase maxima are retained. Historical records remain allocated after their bodies leave active physics. Zero posed_vertices measures CPU debris vertex posing, not per-instance transform updates.

acceptance.scope: Measured bounded offscreen throughput cadence; no GPU-duration, presentation, or input-latency budget claim.

tested_source_scope: Top-level acceptance describes reactive-source production kit runs. historical_production_runs preserves the earlier accepted production runs on 46cf41188b; original serial and intermediate DAE failures remain unchanged.

pixel_readback.timing_scope: Every simulation frame calls the primary renderer once, advances history and exposure, and enters phase statistics without outlier filtering. Any initial exposure warm-up submissions drain before primary frame 0; their count and timing policy appear in submission_timing. Encode timing includes validation, fitting, uploads, encoding, submission, and optional diagnostics. The wait column includes oldest-submission admission in bounded mode, current completion in serial mode, and selected pixel copy/mapping/extraction. Unselected frames omit pixel operations. Pipelined PNG writes and progress logs occur after final drain; serial captures retain their historical writes. Repeated comparisons and extra readbacks are excluded from the historical component sum but retained in continuous iteration timing. Temporal comparisons remain serial and preserve all-frame pixel readback and warmed paired intervals.

submission_timing.warmup_method: This stage required no separate exposure warm-up submissions.
submission_timing.frame_ms_method: Continuous host iteration intervals, including simulation, camera and mesh preparation, encoding, submission, admission and artifact readback waits, retained-pixel copies, and bookkeeping. Adjacent starts bound each interval; the last ends after final drain. Every frame enters p99/max without filtering, retaining the 16.7 ms live budget. This is bounded throughput cadence; frame completion latency is reported separately.
submission_timing.completion_method: One callback per primary submission records the host observation after GPU completion. Callbacks can be delayed until submit/poll; observed latency is an upper bound, not GPU duration. Submitted and completed frame indices must match exactly. All frames submit once; no presentation, vsync, compositor, or dropped-frame behavior is simulated. Native surface latency 2 is a backend hint; this offscreen run explicitly caps pending primary submissions at 2.

intermediate_methods.scope: Seven failed DAE High captures remain retained. Current production runs are separate under current_runs.
intermediate_methods.serial: The original reports use tick plus dynamic mesh plus encode/submit plus current-frame completion wait. They differ in all-frame versus selected pixel extraction, and retain their original reports and acceptance results.
intermediate_methods.bounded: Every simulation frame advances and submits once. At most two primary submissions remain pending. Frame time is the actual adjacent-start host cadence, with the final interval ending after the drain. It includes admission waits and selected artifact readbacks. Observed completion latency is reported separately; no CPU/GPU overlap estimate replaces elapsed time.
intermediate_methods.profiles: Development and production release profiles are recorded per run. Sources, native indirect admission, and profiles differ. No cross-profile or cross-policy speed percentage is claimed.
intermediate_methods.sampling: All 960 raw ledger rows remain in each copied capture.json, including startup and tail. Phase p99 values are recomputed from those rows. Four selected primary readbacks occur at 120, 469, 600, and 900; no frame or outlier is removed.
intermediate_methods.gpu: These ordinary captures disable timestamp diagnostics. The feature support flag is retained separately. Wall cadence and callback observation are not GPU duration and do not simulate vsync or a compositor.

intermediate_artifact_checks.scope: Original five intermediate runs; the two added caster histories and current runs carry their own artifact_checks.

capture.final_asset_override: VERSE_KIT_PACK points to the previously reviewed DAE kit; VERSE_KIT_UNPINNED=1 permits it because the current published kit pin was unavailable. The current kit pin is not tested.
capture.timing_scope: Every simulation frame enters statistics. Frame is tick + dynamic mesh + encode + completion wait. Encode includes uploads and submission. Selected artifact frames also copy/map/extract pixels. PNG writes are outside the sample; no outliers are filtered. The first sample includes exposure warm-up.
capture.comparison_limits: Baseline, first, optimized, and final legacy read pixels every frame. Final selected reads artifact frames and waits for completion without pixels on other frames. No cross-policy percentage improvement is claimed. Baseline lasts 14s; later runs last 16s, so aftermath windows differ. Final also enables TAA, absent from the 10935 baseline.

visual_review.limitations: Fire and smoke obscure some contacts. This assessment covers only the selected stills and does not claim a matched historical comparison or a GPU-duration budget.
